title: Fix negative invoice line-items produced when customers swap between reserved and on-demand tiers mid-cycle
creator: Asha Patel
description: When customers swap plan tiers mid-billing-cycle (e.g., reserved GPU capacity -> on-demand or vice versa), the export reconciler sometimes emits negative invoice line-items in Stripe and NetSuite. Symptoms: duplicated negative lines, net-zero totals that confuse accounting, and downstream bookkeeping failures for customers using synced ERP. This ticket scopes the investigation and provides a fix that ensures deterministic, idempotent export lines and correct proration calculations across timezones and burst-credit adjustments.
reproduction_steps: Create customer with reserved capacity plan starting 2025-02-01 and a monthly billing cycle
Mid-cycle (2025-02-14) switch the plan to on-demand via the Console or API
Generate usage spikes tied to burst credits and rate-limit credits in the same day as swap
Run the billing export reconciler for the affected billing window and inspect generated Stripe invoice line items and NetSuite export payload
investigation_notes: Observed negative line-item creation when a mid-cycle plan swap triggers both a proration adjustment and a separate burst-credit reversal for the same timestamp window
Root triggers appear when two reconciler flows (proration delta and credit backfill) run concurrently and create overlapping invoice lines without deterministic merge keys

Issue is exacerbated by local-time anchoring: customers in non-UTC zones produce hour buckets that cause the reconciler to attribute events to adjacent billing windows leading to cancellations + re-adds
Existing idempotency keys are based on invoice_line+timestamp but not normalized for plan_variant or credit_type, leading to double-apply on retries
root_cause: Race between proration adjustment job and late-usage/credit backfill job plus insufficiently granular idempotency/merge semantics. Timezone-aware bucketing mismatch causes the same logical adjustment to be emitted twice with different bucket timestamps, and reserved/on-demand swap logic does not canonicalize plan lineage for export signatures.
proposed_fix: Canonicalize export signatures: include canonical_plan_id, plan_mode (reserved|on-demand), and credit_category (burst|rate_limit|promo) when computing invoice export idempotency_key
Normalize event bucketing to UTC-aligned anchor for export reconciliation, but keep per-customer timezone for UI reporting only

Introduce a short transactional merge window (5 minutes) where proration and credit backfill ops for the same customer+billing_window are deduped and coalesced into a single export line with explicit narrative
Add a compensating job that scans the last 7 days of exports and replaces negative-line-item anomalies with consolidated lines while preserving audit trail (old lines marked with export_anomaly flag)
Add unit + integration tests covering: mid-cycle swaps, concurrent proration+credit backfill, DST boundaries, and retry storms
acceptance_criteria: Exports no longer produce duplicated negative invoice lines for the same logical adjustment in the reproduced scenarios
E2E test in CI simulates a mid-cycle swap and asserts a single proration adjustment export line per billing window
Backfill/compensate job can detect and mark prior anomalous exports and produce corrected export payloads without altering customer-visible invoice totals
No regressions in existing billing export signatures (backwards-compatible: old exports still parse)
rollout_plan: Feature branch with tests -> internal review -> staging rollout to billing-staging cluster
Deploy reconciler changes behind feature flag 'dedupe_proration_credit' in staging; run the reconciler for rolling windows and compare staging vs production exports
Run compensating scan in read-only mode to capture anomalies and generate proposed correction report for finance team
Enable dedupe_proration_credit in production during low-traffic window; monitor for export error rates and accounting diffs; keep rollback plan ready
After 72 hours of stable metrics, run the compensating job to fix any historical anomalies in the last 30 days (with finance approval)
monitoring_queries: billing.exports.latency.p95 and p99 after enabling dedupe_proration_credit
finance.invoice.reconciliation.failures count for NetSuite and Stripe syncs
alert: any increase >5% in export_failure_rate after rollout
tests: Unit: idempotency key computation includes canonical_plan_id and credit_category
Integration: simulate concurrent proration+credit backfill and assert single export line
Regression: DST boundary simulation for customers in America/Sao_Paulo and Asia/Tokyo
Backfill dry-run: safe mode run produces correction candidates without writing to NetSuite/Stripe
notes_for_finance: Finance: compensating job will create corrected export payloads with an audit mapping. We will not reissue customer invoices automatically; ops will review before pushing NetSuite corrections. Prepare a reconciliation window and expect small manual adjustments for three enterprise customers in NA during the first backfill run.
next_steps: Run feature flag in staging for 48 hours and generate comparison report
Schedule finance review meeting for 2025-03-10 to approve backfill run
Post-mortem doc to be published under the Confluence link after production verification
